title: Morning movement
tomorrow: a poet sits in a ruined city. what does he say is new every morning?

segments.voice: Yesterday, today I will: the hadith of intentions, the same road to Medina and two different journeys. An aim lives in the heart. Today the morning gets a body.

Some mornings the body wakes up stiff and the mind wakes up anxious, and coffee only fixes one of them. Henry David Thoreau, living in his small cabin by Walden Pond, wrote down what he did with his mornings: "I got up early and bathed in the pond; that was a religious exercise, and one of the best things which I did." A religious exercise. Not a workout. Why would a swim count as that?
screen: `STIFF BODY, ANXIOUS MIND.` → `A CABIN BY WALDEN POND.` → `A RELIGIOUS EXERCISE?`

segments.voice: Thoreau was one of the Transcendentalists, New England writers who looked for the sacred directly in nature and in the self, not only in churches and creeds. For him, dawn was holy time. Just before the line about the pond, he says he worshipped Aurora, the dawn, as sincerely as the Greeks did. A few paragraphs on comes this line: "Morning is when I am awake and there is a dawn in me." So the clock doesn't decide when it's morning. Waking up does. And for Thoreau, waking up went through the body: the pond, then the woods. In his essay on walking he says he couldn't keep his health and spirits without sauntering through the woods and fields, free of the world's business. Here is the teaching, named plainly. The Transcendentalists held that nature is a direct way to the sacred, met with the body and the senses, not only with ideas. The dawn pond was worship because it woke Thoreau to a world he found holy. That's the difference from a fitness routine, which aims at the body for the body's sake. Thoreau's swim aimed through the body at being awake. On your own path, tag still on: move first, not to burn anything, but to arrive. A stretch, a walk around the block, a bow to the light, done the way Thoreau did his pond.
screen: `THE SACRED, MET IN NATURE.` · `A WORSHIPPER OF THE DAWN.` · `MORNING IS WHEN I AM AWAKE.` · `THROUGH THE BODY, TO BEING AWAKE.` · then, large: `MOVE FIRST.`

segments.voice: Stand and stretch slowly toward the ceiling, then let your arms fall and roll your shoulders back. If there's a window, turn your face toward it, the way Thoreau turned to the dawn, and let whatever light there is reach you. Let it be your small version of Thoreau's pond: a way of waking up, not a workout.
Morning movement: moving first, to wake up rather than to work out. For Thoreau, a dawn swim was a religious exercise.
Keep this one: move first, and let the body wake the rest of you. See you in the morning.
